tex_content.html:
\begin{equation} P_{T_1,w_1}(t)= w_1\left(\frac{1+4t}{1+4T_1}\right)^{3/4} +2\pi (1+4T_1)^{1/4}(1+4t)^{3/4}-2\pi (1+4t). \end{equation} It satisfies $P'= -2\pi +3P/(1+4t)$ and $P(T_1)=w_1$ for $t\geq T_1$.
Proof

Multiplying the ODE by $(1+4t)^{-3/4}$ gives derivative $-2\pi (1+4t)^{-3/4}$, whose integral is $-2\pi ((1+4t)^{1/4}-(1+4T_1)^{1/4})$. Solving for $P$ gives (4) and $P(T_1)=w_1$. All real powers have positive arguments.

□
